payload.rationale: The August 2026 unemployment rate was 4.1%, and the Fed's median Q4 projection is also 4.1%. To resolve Yes, the October rate must reach 4.4% or higher, requiring an increase of at least 0.3 percentage points over just two months. While June and July payrolls were revised down significantly (31k and 21k), August rebounded to 162k, making a sudden spike to >4.3% less likely but not impossible if the summer weakness resumes. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the August payroll rebound and Fed projections suggest stability, meaning the rate could easily stay around 4.1%. The strongest reason it could be too low is that the weak June/July payrolls could indicate an underlying deterioration that accelerates in the fall, outpacing the Fed's expectations.
limitations: Only three recent payroll readings are included. September and October survey results are unknown.
A Q4 unemployment projection is a quarterly average, not the October reading; payroll employment and unemployment come from different surveys.
Small coordinator-selected packet; no fitted probability model or complete research review.
